nodes.label: Dependency Inversion Rule ("the one rule that matters")
nodes.rationale: Lets networking/data sources/AI providers get swapped later without touching UI or business logic — described as the whole architectural point of the project, not incidental style.
nodes.norm_label: dependency inversion rule ("the one rule that matters")

nodes.label: Moya (over Alamofire) networking layer
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it's a well-known convention an AI agent will recognize rather than guessing at a bespoke layer.

nodes.label: Firebase Cloud Functions backend
nodes.rationale: Holds Gemini API and Google Places API keys server-side so they are never embedded in the client app; client calls the Cloud Function, not the third-party APIs directly.

nodes.label: Google Places API
nodes.rationale: Cost-sensitive: hard usage/quota caps must be configured server-side.

nodes.label: Gemini API
nodes.rationale: Cost-sensitive: hard usage/quota caps must be configured server-side; one Gemini call returns the hero pick plus specialty picks.

nodes.label: "I'm Hungry" one-screen one-button flow
nodes.rationale: No login, no search bar, no list-of-results dashboard — a decision tool for tourists unfamiliar with the local food scene, not a directory.

nodes.label: Working style with project owner (Sadri)
nodes.rationale: If a decision looks technically, financially, or strategically questionable, say so directly and invite debate rather than silently complying — explicitly requested by the owner.
